authority: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)

description.en: Third-party motor vehicle insurance is mandatory for all vehicles plying on Indian roads under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. It covers liability arising from injury or death of a third party, or damage to third-party property, caused by or arising out of the use of the insured vehicle. IRDAI regulates premium rates for the third-party component.

verifiedConditions.claim: The vehicle must be registered with a Regional Transport Office (RTO) under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988. Insurance is mandatory for all motor vehicles operating on public roads.
A valid Registration Certificate (RC) is required to obtain motor vehicle insurance. The RC contains vehicle details used for premium calculation.

unverifiedEligibility: Commercial vehicles may require additional coverage beyond basic third-party insurance.
Electric vehicles may have different premium rates under recent IRDAI guidelines.
Vehicles older than 15 years may face difficulty obtaining comprehensive insurance but third-party remains mandatory.
Imported or modified vehicles may require special insurance assessment.

requirements.claim: Registration Certificate (RC) of the vehicle containing engine number, chassis number, registration number, and owner details.
Identity proof of the vehicle owner — Aadhaar card, PAN card, voter ID, or passport.
Address proof of the vehicle owner for communication and policy issuance.
Previous insurance policy details for renewal — policy number, expiry date, and no-claim bonus (NCB) details if applicable for comprehensive policies.
Vehicle inspection may be required if the previous policy has lapsed for more than 90 days or if the vehicle is being insured for the first time after a gap.

processInformation.claim: Select an IRDAI-authorized general insurance company. Third-party motor insurance can be purchased from any authorized insurer — online through the insurer's website, through an insurance agent, or at the insurer's branch office.

Provide vehicle details (registration number, engine number, chassis number, make and model, year of manufacture, fuel type) and owner details (name, address, contact). For online purchase, these are entered into the insurer's web portal.
Pay the premium amount as per IRDAI-notified rates for the third-party component. Payment can be made online (net banking, UPI, card) or offline at insurer's office.

The insurance policy is issued immediately upon successful premium payment. The digital policy document is sent via email and can be downloaded from the insurer's portal. A physical copy can also be requested.

output.claim: A Motor Vehicle Insurance Policy document is issued containing the policy number, insured vehicle details, coverage period (typically one year), premium paid, and coverage details. The policy is valid as proof of insurance under the Motor Vehicles Act and must be carried while driving.

fees.applicability: Third-party premium for two-wheelers (exceeding 350cc) as per IRDAI notification
fees.claim: Third-party insurance premiums for two-wheelers are fixed by IRDAI. For vehicles not exceeding 75cc: Rs. 538; 75cc-150cc: Rs. 714; 150cc-350cc: Rs. 1,366; exceeding 350cc: Rs. 2,804. Rates are revised periodically by IRDAI.

fees.applicability: Third-party premium for private cars as per IRDAI notification
fees.claim: Third-party insurance premiums for private cars vary by engine capacity. Not exceeding 1000cc: Rs. 2,094; 1000cc-1500cc: Rs. 3,416; exceeding 1500cc: Rs. 6,521. Electric vehicles have separate rate schedules.

processingTime.applicability: Motor insurance policy issuance from application to receipt
processingTime.claim: Motor vehicle insurance policies are issued instantly upon premium payment when purchased online. Offline purchases through agents or branch offices may take up to one working day for policy issuance.

sources.title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India — Official Portal
sources.publisher: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
sources.evidenceExcerpt: IRDAI regulates the insurance sector in India and notifies third-party motor insurance premium rates annually. The portal provides guidelines on motor insurance, list of authorized insurers, and consumer grievance mechanisms.
claimsSupported: Third-party motor insurance is mandatory under Motor Vehicles Act.
IRDAI fixes third-party premium rates by vehicle category.
Insurance policies can be purchased online for instant issuance.
Vehicle RC details are required for insurance.
sources.uncertainty: Premium rates are revised annually by IRDAI. The quoted figures may change with new notifications.

sources.title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 — Section 146 (Necessity for insurance)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 mandates that no person shall use or cause or allow any other person to use a motor vehicle in a public place unless there is a policy of insurance in force. Penalty for driving without insurance is a fine up to Rs. 2,000 and/or imprisonment up to 3 months.
claimsSupported: Motor vehicle insurance is legally mandatory for all vehicles on public roads.
Driving without insurance attracts fine and imprisonment.
sources.uncertainty: Penalty amounts and imprisonment terms may be updated through amendments.

limitations: This record covers mandatory third-party motor insurance. Comprehensive/own-damage coverage is optional and has variable pricing.
Premium rates are notified annually by IRDAI and the figures cited may be outdated.
Commercial vehicle insurance premiums are significantly different and not covered in detail here.
Long-term (3-year and 5-year) third-party policies have different premium structures.
State-specific surcharges or taxes on insurance premiums are not modeled.
Claims process and settlement procedures are not covered in this record.

review.reviewReason: IRDAI premium rates need annual verification as they are revised each year. Current rates cited need confirmation against latest notification.
nextReviewTrigger: Annual IRDAI notification revising third-party premium rates.
Amendments to Motor Vehicles Act affecting insurance requirements.
Introduction of new vehicle categories or electric vehicle-specific rates.
Changes in penalty provisions for uninsured vehicles.
